finding: Model parallelism reduces per-device parameter memory by partitioning model weights across devices.
evidence: Ideal partitioned memory scales as total_parameter_memory / num_devices.
why_it_matters: This allows larger models to fit when one device cannot hold the full model.

finding: Effective memory reduction is lower than ideal scaling because of overhead.
evidence: The simulation includes 8.0% combined replication and communication overhead.
why_it_matters: Real model parallelism is not perfectly linear.

finding: Two-device partitioning gives useful but limited memory reduction.
evidence: Average fp32 effective per-device reduction at 2 devices is 42.00%.
why_it_matters: Two devices help, but overhead still consumes a visible part of memory.

finding: Four and eight devices provide stronger per-device memory reduction.
evidence: Average fp32 effective reduction is 67.00% at 4 devices and 79.50% at 8 devices.
why_it_matters: More devices reduce per-device weight storage, but communication and replication costs remain.

finding: This is analytical model-parallel planning, not real distributed profiling.
evidence: No tensor parallelism, pipeline parallelism, NCCL communication, or multi-GPU runtime was executed.
why_it_matters: The results should be presented as memory-estimation logic, not measured distributed performance.
